name: CAPRICORN
question: Do once-daily mirabegron 25 mg and 50 mg reduce incontinence and micturition frequency versus placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.blinding: double-blind after a single-blind placebo run-in
design.population: Adults with overactive bladder symptoms for at least three months, at least eight micturitions and three grade 3 or 4 urgency episodes per 24 hours after a two-week placebo run-in; predominant stress incontinence was excluded.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 314; Results, p 315

verdictNote: Both coprimary endpoints met for both doses at 12 weeks; 25 mg missed the first key secondary endpoint.
takeaway: In adults with overactive bladder, mirabegron 25 mg and 50 mg once daily improved 12-week incontinence episodes and micturition frequency versus placebo. The 50 mg dose also improved voided volume; 25 mg did not meet that key secondary endpoint.

reports.label: 12-week randomized results
reports.citation: Herschorn S, Barkin J, Castro-Diaz D, et al. "A Phase III, Randomized, Double-blind, Parallel-group, Placebo-controlled, Multicentre Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of the β3 Adrenoceptor Agonist, Mirabegron, in Patients With Symptoms of Overactive Bladder." *Urology.* 2013;82(2):313-320. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2013.02.077
reports.followUp: 12 weeks of randomized treatment; safety follow-up two weeks later

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to final visit in mean episodes per 24 hours, FAS-I
results.note: Effect is 50 mg minus placebo. For 25 mg, difference -0.40 (95% CI -0.74 to -0.06; P=0.005). Both dose comparisons met the prespecified multiplicity-adjusted threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Results, p 315

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to final visit in mean micturitions per 24 hours, FAS
results.note: Effect is 50 mg minus placebo. For 25 mg, difference -0.47 (95% CI -0.82 to -0.13; P=0.007). Both dose comparisons met the prespecified multiplicity-adjusted threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Results, p 315

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to final visit in mean volume voided per micturition, mL, FAS
results.note: 25 mg minus placebo; this comparison missed the prespecified threshold, stopping the gate for subsequent 25 mg key secondary endpoints.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Results, p 315

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to final visit in mean volume voided per micturition, mL, FAS
results.note: 50 mg minus placebo; met the prespecified key secondary threshold. The 25 mg comparison is recorded separately.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Results, p 315

results.endpoint: Incontinence episodes per 24 hours at week 4
results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to week 4 in mean episodes per 24 hours, FAS-I
results.note: Effect is 50 mg minus placebo and met the gatekeeping threshold. For 25 mg, nominal difference -0.34 (95% CI -0.68 to -0.01; P=0.039); its gate had stopped at voided volume.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Results, p 315

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to week 4 in mean micturitions per 24 hours, FAS
results.note: Effect is 50 mg minus placebo; P=0.035 did not meet the 0.025 gatekeeping threshold. The 25 mg nominal difference was -0.18 (95% CI -0.53 to +0.16; P=0.30), after its gate had stopped.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 316; Methods, Statistical Analysis, p 314

results.measure: Adjusted change from baseline to final visit in treatment-satisfaction visual analog scale, FAS
results.note: Effect is 50 mg minus placebo. For 25 mg, TS-VAS difference +0.49 (95% CI +0.07 to +0.91; P=0.024). OAB-q symptom bother differed for 50 mg by -2.8 (95% CI -5.3 to -0.3; P=0.028) and for 25 mg by -1.8 (95% CI -4.3 to +0.7; P=0.15). These patient-reported tests were additional secondary analyses outside the gatekeeping hierarchy. Neither OAB-q HRQL total score nor PPBC differed significantly from placebo.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 317; Results, p 315

harms.label: Treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 318; Safety Assessments, p 315
harms.note: Safety analysis set. Severe treatment-emergent events: 8/432 (1.9%), 8/440 (1.8%), and 16/433 (3.7%), respectively. Hypertension preferred-term events: 49/432 (11.3%), 47/440 (10.7%), and 37/433 (8.5%).

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Treatment-emergent urinary tract infection, safety analysis set.

harms.label: Urinary retention and elevated post-void residual
harms.note: Retention was an adverse event. PVR values refer to the final visit; the paper does not give a final-visit denominator.

delivery.label: Drug regimen and completion
delivery.value: Mirabegron 25 mg, mirabegron 50 mg, or matching placebo once daily for 12 weeks after a two-week single-blind placebo run-in; 46/433 (10.6%), 54/440 (12.3%), and 66/433 (15.2%), respectively, discontinued treatment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 314; Safety Assessments and Figure 1, p 317-318
delivery.note: Safety follow-up was two weeks after the final treatment visit.

relations.note: Same phase III mirabegron registration program; SCORPIO tested 50 and 100 mg in Europe and Australia.
Same phase III mirabegron registration program; ARIES tested 50 and 100 mg in the United States and Canada.
